q.t: Science is best described as…
o: A way of thinking, observing and doing things
q.e: Science is a step-by-step way to find answers to questions.

q.t: What is the first step of the scientific method?
q.e: Observe → Question → Guess → Test → Analyse.

q.t: What is the last step of the scientific method?
q.e: After testing, you analyse what the result means.

q.t: Your pen stops writing. 'Why did my pen stop?' is the…
q.e: Noticing it stopped is the observation; asking why is the question.

q.t: 'The ink is finished' is a…
q.e: It's a possible answer you can test.

q.t: Opening the pen to check the refill is the…
q.e: You test the guess by checking.

q.t: Who can do science?
o: Anyone who follows the scientific method
q.e: Scientists follow the method — but so can anyone.

q.t: Where can science be found?
q.e: Science is everywhere around us.

q.t: The only planet we know that supports life is…
q.e: That's why we must protect Earth's environment.

q.t: Science is compared to a…
q.e: Every discovery adds a piece — and raises more questions.

q.t: Order the steps: Test, Observe, Analyse, Question, Guess.
q.e: Observe → Question → Guess → Test → Analyse.

q.t: The refill is NOT empty. What should you do?
o: Make a new guess and test it
Say the first guess was right
Buy a new pen without thinking
q.e: A wrong guess removes one possibility; guess again.

q.t: Why is a wrong guess not a failure?
q.e: Each wrong guess narrows down the answer.

q.t: Sometimes a puzzle piece is in the wrong place. In science this means…
o: New discoveries can change our understanding
q.e: Being willing to move a piece is part of doing science well.

q.t: Every new discovery usually…
q.e: The puzzle is unending.

q.t: Measuring body temperature during a fever belongs to which topic?
q.e: Heat covers hot and cold and measuring temperature.

q.t: Learning how to separate materials belongs to which topic?
q.e: Materials: what things are made of and how to separate them.

q.t: The Sun, Moon and stars belong to which topic?
q.e: The book's last topic looks outward to space.

q.t: Groundbreaking discoveries often come from…
q.e: Science is everywhere, so discoveries can come from anywhere.

q.t: The scientific method is a…
q.e: If the guess is wrong, go back and guess again.

q.t: A torch doesn't light. Which is a good 'guess' step?
q.e: A guess is a possible answer that can be tested.

q.t: In the torch example, which is the 'test'?
o: Put new batteries in and switch on
q.e: Testing checks whether the guess explains the problem.

q.t: With new batteries the torch still doesn't light. Analysis:
o: The battery guess was wrong; try another guess
q.e: Go back and guess again — maybe the bulb is broken.

q.t: Why does the book cover such different topics?
q.e: Living things, food, water, heat and materials all link up.

q.t: Which is an observation?
o: The plant's leaves are turning yellow
q.e: An observation is what you notice.

q.t: Which is a question?
o: Why are the leaves turning yellow?
I moved it to the window
q.e: A question asks why or how.

q.t: Moving the plant into sunlight to see if it improves is a…
q.e: You're checking the guess that it needs light.

q.t: What makes someone a scientist?
q.e: It's the method, not the costume.

q.t: Why should we protect Earth's environment?
o: It's the only planet known to support life
q.e: We have nowhere else to live.

q.t: If a discovery shows an old idea was wrong, a good scientist…
q.e: Moving a misplaced puzzle piece is part of good science.

q.t: Your milk smells sour. Which order of thinking is scientific?
o: Notice smell → ask why → guess it's old → check the date → decide
Throw it away and forget it
q.e: That follows Observe → Question → Guess → Test → Analyse.

q.t: Two guesses for a dead pen: 'ink finished' and 'ink dried'. Which do you test first?
o: The easiest to check — look at the refill
q.e: Testing removes possibilities one by one; start with the easy check.

q.t: Why isn't science 'only doing experiments'?
o: It also needs observing, questioning, guessing and analysing
q.e: The experiment is just the test step in a longer process.

q.t: A friend says 'science is finished — we know everything'. What would you reply?
q.e: The jigsaw puzzle is unending.

q.t: Which topic would explain why it rains?
q.e: The water topic covers rain, freezing and boiling.

q.t: Which step answers 'was my guess right?'
q.e: Analysing the test result tells you.

q.t: A good guess must be…
q.e: You must be able to check it, or the method can't continue.

q.t: The scientific method is useful in daily life because…
o: It helps solve everyday problems step by step
q.e: You already use it when something stops working.

q.t: Which is NOT part of science?
o: Refusing to change your mind with new evidence
q.e: Science requires changing ideas when evidence shows they're wrong.

q.t: After analysing, if the guess was right, you have…
o: Found an answer to your question
To start with a new observation always
q.e: A confirmed guess answers the question — until new evidence appears.
